statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail sits in the low band while Stress stays elevated on an energy- and rates-driven backdrop.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold: the cash Nasdaq-100 closed -1.39% but roughly 170 points above its session low, and NQ futures have recovered about 0.5% overnight, so retracement is still functioning. The elevated Stress reading describes a difficult high-volatility environment - Brent above 100, a 10-year near 5.25%, and an unresolved AI-revenue repricing - rather than an observed mean-reversion failure. The narrow 13:30Z-15:00Z danger window covers the US cash open and the Michigan preliminary release.
headline: NQ futures recover overnight after an orderly AI-led cash decline; Tail low, Stress elevated
body: The cash Nasdaq-100 closed Thursday at 30,725.81, down 434.27 points or 1.39%, in a session range of 30,556.40 to 31,125.13 - a second consecutive decline, but one that finished roughly 170 points above the low. The trigger was a Financial Times report that OpenAI's annualised revenue was approaching 50 billion dollars at end-September against about 70 billion previously indicated, a difference largely attributable to how the figure is calculated rather than to lost sales. AI-linked names repriced sharply: Oracle fell about 5% to near 136.50 with its 300 billion dollar OpenAI cloud commitment representing roughly 45% of backlog, Broadcom lost close to 4%, AMD about 3%, and a semiconductor gauge fell about 3.4%. Energy and rates amplified the move. Brent settled at 104.28, up 4%, and WTI at 91.49, up 3.6%, with European diesel futures up 6%, on Hormuz vessel-attack reports, Houthi-claimed strikes on Saudi airports and Hurricane Isaias disruption to Gulf of Mexico operations. The 10-year yield traded through 5.35% intraday before settling near 5.23-5.28%, against a 4.77% two-year and a 3.88% effective funds rate. A Truth Social post stating that the United States will not attack Iran before the 3 November midterms, with the blockade left in place, produced only a brief oil dip. Current structure is two-sided rather than pathological: NQ futures trade near 31,130, about 0.5% higher, inside a narrow 30,953 to 31,138 overnight band; VIX is 15.41; and the Asian session closed split, with the Hang Seng Tech index up about 1.6% against a Nikkei down 0.8% and a Shanghai Composite down 1.4%. No persistent one-way NQ structure, shallow-pullback sequence or failed-retracement pattern has been observed, so Tail is held at 18 while Stress reflects the energy, rates and AI-narrative stack. Shared Finviz context was not usable this run: the file carries a 2026-09-29 collection timestamp and a partial collection status, well outside the 90-minute freshness limit, so the assessment rests entirely on independent research.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry a published Claude assessment. The window opens green with Tail near 11 and Stress in the low 50s, deteriorates through the European and US morning as the AI-revenue story and the energy move developed - Tail reaching the watch band from 07:00Z and peaking at 28 with Stress 72 in the 17:00Z hour, the only orange slot - then improves steadily after the US close. The last eight hours are green with Tail between 16 and 18 and Stress decaying from 65 to 55, consistent with retracement resuming once the cash session ended.
outlookSummary: The horizon splits into a live session and a weekend halt. Through the European morning Tail oscillates between 19 and 21 on liquidity transitions rather than observed structure. It rises to 23 in the 13:00Z hour containing the US cash open and peaks at 24 in the 14:00Z hour, where the Michigan preliminary sentiment and inflation-expectations release overlaps an unwinding opening auction - the narrow 13:30Z-15:00Z danger window. Escalation beyond the watch band would require actually observed opening-auction continuation with shallow pullbacks, in the Aug 4 pattern; an orderly print with visible retracement instead argues for a quick step down. A secondary rise to 22 covers the power hour into the 20:00Z cash close, where Friday weekend-risk reduction and the Fed Collins speech meet a thin book. From 21:00Z the CME weekend halt removes any tradable price path, so Tail collapses to 10-12 and Confidence steps down to around 70 to reflect the absence of live price-path evidence; the unresolved Iran blockade, Hormuz vessel reports and Hurricane Isaias supply disruption convert into Sunday reopen-gap exposure rather than intraday path risk.

Retracement is functioning and VIX sits near 15.4, so Tail stays low while energy and rates keep Stress elevated.
